tasks.short: Sort out damaged or defective items, get write-off or vendor return agreed, then dispose or ship back.

steps.what: Stocker spots damaged or defective items while receiving or filling shelves
Stocker decides dispose, markdown or return to vendor: from the printed return list today; from the route the vendor's terms allow on the handheld after the change
Stocker takes a photo of the damaged item with the handheld
Stocker writes item, quantity and damage reason on the damage log sheet
Supervisor checks the day's damage records before posting: item, quantity, reason, photo and value match, and approves write-offs above the limit
Write-off posting: the stock administrator keys each write-off today; after the change the supervisor releases the checked write-offs and the workflow posts them to the stock system
Supervisor checks each return request before release: item, quantity, photo and the vendor's terms match, and it goes to the right vendor contact or portal
Vendor return request: the stock administrator e-mails it today; after the change the supervisor releases each checked request with its photo to the vendor
Stocker packs and labels return items for vendor pickup
Stocker disposes of written-off items in the right waste stream

tasks.design: A damage form on the handheld scanner, configured in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, takes the item scan, quantity, reason code and photo, and shows the route the vendor's terms allow (return, destroy for credit, write off). The supervisor checks the day's damage records on the handheld, approving write-offs above the limit, and releases the write-offs, which a workflow in the {WORKFLOW} platform posts to the stock system; the supervisor also checks each return request with its photo and releases it to the vendor through the {PARTNER_PORTAL} or {EMAIL}, and the workflow prints the return label.
tasks.previous_blocker: Vendor return terms sat in purchasing files and printed lists, and damage was logged on paper that the office keyed later.
tasks.enabler_now: Handheld scanners already run stock forms, and vendor terms can be held as a few fields per vendor; the routing and e-mail are plain workflow.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether an item is sellable at a markdown stays a person's call; vendors differ in how they accept return requests.
tasks.human_edge: Looking at the item and deciding whether it can still be sold, and handling hazardous or leaking goods safely.

ambition.what: Vendor credit claimed for every eligible damaged item the same day, instead of in a monthly batch that misses deadlines.

tasks.altitude: The stocker records damage once with a scan and photo; the supervisor approves high-value write-offs from the handheld.

reach.role: laborer and freight, stock and material mover
reach.task: Report goods damaged in transit at the dock
reach.learn: Whether one damage form and reason list serves the dock and the shop floor.

evidence.claim: Handheld scanners in warehouse and stock systems can capture write-offs with reason codes and photos.
In the Netherlands, scanners that log each action per person can observe performance, so the works council must consent first.
Waste streams for damaged food, chemicals and electronics follow national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from spotting the damage to the item disposed or shipped back; vendor credit matching in accounts payable is outside.
Input contract: vendor return terms per vendor (return allowed, destroy for credit, credit limit, contact or portal), produced by purchasing in the {PROCUREMENT} system; fallback is the printed list.
Native configuration is tried first: the stock system's write-off form before a separate app.
Supervisor and stock administrator time is outside the stocker's savings.
The physical inspection, packing and disposal do not get faster except the printed label.
s3 is part of keeping damage records, which sibling task 53-7065.00:23894 covers; its saving is counted there, so s3 keeps its full time here.
The stocker's photo (s3p) is new and keeps its full time; s2 keeps 60 because the vendor's route shows on the handheld instead of the printed list.
unknowns: Whether vendor return terms are kept per vendor in any system today.
The write-off limit that needs a supervisor.
research_questions: What share of damaged items is eligible for vendor credit and how much credit is missed today?

already_counted.description: Supervisor approves write-offs above the limit on the handheld.

incremental.description: Stocker fixes scan or photo errors and uses the paper fallback when the handheld is down.
Purchasing keeps vendor return terms current.

approvals.approved_version: The day's write-offs with item, quantity, reason code, photo and value exactly as checked by the supervisor in s4, posted once to the stock system; any edit needs a new check.

Each return request with item, quantity, photo and reason exactly as checked by the supervisor in s8c, sent once to the vendor contact or portal named in the vendor's terms; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many vendors have unclear terms, so routes are still looked up or asked (s2 keeps 85) (4.4); high: vendor terms are complete (8.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Log pre-use checks of pallet trucks, damage to stock or equipment, and consumables used.

steps.what: Stocker checks pallet truck or forklift before use: forks, brakes, battery
Stocker fills the pre-use checklist and equipment use log: on paper today; on the handheld per scanned equipment ID after the change
Stocker checks a failed pre-use check before it goes to maintenance: the defect noted matches what was found, and the truck ID is right
Stocker sends the checked defect to maintenance, which marks the truck out of service
Stocker takes a photo of the damage
Stocker writes a damage report on stock or equipment, what, where and how: on paper today; on the handheld after the change, with item and location from the scan
Shift supervisor reads logs and reports, decides repair, lock-out or claim
Office assistant copies logs and reports into the equipment spreadsheet
Stocker records pallets, wrap and other stock used: on the usage sheet today; by scanning the barcode and entering the quantity used after the change

tasks.design: Forms in the {WORKFLOW} platform on the handheld replace the paper sheets: a pre-use checklist per equipment ID where the stocker checks any fail and sends it to maintenance, which marks the truck out of service, a damage report with scan, location and photo, and a consumables issue by barcode. The form data are the record; a {BI} view shows open defects and damage by equipment and area, not by person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checklists and damage reports were cheap on paper, and nobody owned a system for equipment records.
tasks.enabler_now: Form builders on handhelds take an afternoon to set up and write straight to a table a dashboard can read.
tasks.still_hard: The physical check and honest reporting of who damaged what depend on site culture, not the form.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a fault that is not on the checklist and refusing to drive a truck that feels wrong.

ambition.what: Maintenance planned from defect trends per truck, rather than repairs after breakdowns.

tasks.altitude: The stocker's checks stay; the supervisor decides on lock-outs from live reports instead of a pile of sheets.

reach.role: laborer and freight, stock and material mover
reach.task: Pre-use checks of forklifts and reach trucks
reach.learn: Whether one checklist per equipment type covers both roles.

evidence.claim: Form builders on mobile devices can record checklists with photos and trigger notifications on a fail.
In the Netherlands, tools that log actions per person can observe performance and need works council consent.
A French regulator fined a logistics operator for scanner indicators measuring idle time per worker and keeping them too long.

assumptions: Boundary: from the pre-use check or damage event to the record kept; repairs and insurance claims are outside.
Input contract: equipment ID label, checklist items per equipment type, location code and consumable barcodes, produced by the site manager; fallback is the paper sheet.
Records name the reporter for follow-up but are not used to score people.
Supervisor and office assistant time is outside the stocker's savings.
Pre-use checks follow national workplace safety rules; their content does not change.

Sizing: ticking the checklist and writing the damage report stay first records, so s2 and s3 keep 80 (only the equipment ID, item and location come from the scan); s6 keeps 70 because the barcode names the item and the quantity is still entered. The defect check, its send and the photo keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether equipment carries IDs that a handheld can scan.
Whether a works council has agreed to per-person equipment logs.
research_questions: How many damage events go unreported today, and does an easier form change that?

incremental.description: Stocker answers maintenance questions on reported defects and uses paper when the handheld is down.
Site manager keeps checklists, equipment IDs and the defect view current.

approvals.approved_version: The failed pre-use check with truck ID and defect exactly as checked by the stocker in s2c, sent once to maintenance with the truck marked out of service; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: handhelds are shared or missing, so paper sheets stay for about half of the shift (s2 and s3 keep 90, s6 keeps 85) (6.2); high: handhelds for every stocker (13.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Work out markdown, weight or multi-buy prices for items, label them and report the markdowns.

steps.what: Stocker picks out items to reprice: near expiry, damaged packaging, loose goods
Stocker looks up base price and markdown rule on the handheld or price list; after the change only for loose or unbarcoded goods
Stocker computes the new item or group price with a calculator; after the change only for loose or unbarcoded goods
Stocker checks the reduced price before printing: item, new price and date fit the markdown rule and the item's condition
Stocker prints the checked price sticker and fixes it to the item: written by hand today
Stocker lists the markdowns on a sheet for the store office
Store office keys markdowns into the till price file

tasks.design: A markdown function on the handheld, configured in the {OPS_SYSTEM}: the stocker scans the item and picks days to expiry or a condition code, the agreed markdown rule sets the price, and the belt printer issues a reduced-price barcode that the {OTHER} point-of-sale till reads directly. Each markdown is logged with item, old and new price, so the markdown sheet and the office keying disappear.
tasks.previous_blocker: Markdown rules lived in a printed table, and the till only knew the base price, so every reduced price had to be computed and keyed twice.
tasks.enabler_now: Reduced-price barcodes and handheld label printers are standard, and the rule is a short table.
tasks.still_hard: Loose goods without a barcode and one-off judgement prices still need a person; rules must match price-indication law.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which items will not sell in time and deciding when a markdown is worth more than a write-off.

ambition.what: Markdowns checked twice a day on every near-expiry line, not once at closing.

tasks.altitude: The stocker scans and labels instead of calculating; the rule table owner decides the steps of each markdown.

reach.task: Ring up items with reduced-price stickers
reach.learn: Whether the price barcode removes price disputes at the till.

evidence.claim: Stock systems with handheld printers can apply a markdown rule and print a reduced-price barcode the till reads.
EU price indication rules require the selling price and unit price to be shown; announced reductions must show the prior lowest price, with national exemptions possible for perishable goods.

assumptions: Boundary: from picking items to reprice to the labelled item on the shelf with the price known to the till; base price setting is outside.
Input contract: markdown rule table (category, days to expiry or condition code, percentage, minimum price), produced by the commercial team; fallback is the printed table and a handwritten sticker.
Native configuration is tried first: the stock or till system's markdown function before custom code.
Prices outside the rule are refused by the handheld and go to the supervisor's existing price override, outside this task.
Store office time is outside the stocker's savings.
About 85% of repriced items carry a barcode; for loose and unbarcoded goods the stocker still looks up and computes the price, so s2 and s3 keep 15. The check before printing keeps its full time.
unknowns: Whether the till reads price-embedded barcodes today.
How many reprices a stocker does per shift.
research_questions: What share of repricing is loose goods without barcodes?

incremental.description: Stocker handles printer faults and items the rule refuses.
Commercial team keeps the markdown rule table current.

approvals.approved_version: The reduced-price label with item, new price and date exactly as checked by the stocker in s4c, printed once as a barcode the till reads and fixed to that item; any change needs a new check and label.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many loose or unbarcoded goods keep half of the lookups and sums by hand (s2 and s3 keep 50) (36.6); high: 85% of items scan as assumed (49.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Ring up a customer's merchandise at the till, total it and take cash or card.

steps.what: Customer puts merchandise on the checkout counter
Stocker scans each item, keys unbarcoded items and weighs loose goods
Stocker resolves missing barcodes or price queries by checking the shelf or a colleague
Stocker totals the sale and takes cash with change or starts card payment
Customer pays by card or hands over cash
Stocker hands over receipt and bags the merchandise

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} point-of-sale till so item search by name and a list of today's price changes answer most price queries at the counter, and link the card terminal so the total goes across without rekeying. Scanning, cash handling and bagging stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Little blocked it; the till already totals the sale, and the remaining effort is physical.
tasks.enabler_now: Most tills support item search by description and integrated card terminals as settings.
tasks.still_hard: Scanning, weighing and cash handling are physical; self-checkout shifts work to customers and raises loss, so it is not assumed here.
tasks.human_edge: Serving the customer, spotting a wrong price or an unscanned item, and handling cash honestly.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; fewer interruptions to fetch a price.

reach.task: Process merchandise returns at the till
reach.learn: Whether the same item search speeds returns without a receipt.

evidence.claim: Tills can search items by description and pass the total to an integrated card terminal.
Card payment data at the till falls under GDPR for the personal data it holds; acceptance of cash follows national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from items on the counter to the customer leaving with a receipt; till closing is outside.
Input contract: item master with barcode, description and current price, produced by the commercial team in the till's price file; fallback is a shelf check.
The till's own totalling earns no saving; only price queries and card rekeying change.
Customer time is outside the stocker's savings.
unknowns: Whether card terminals are already integrated with the till.
How often stockers staff the till.
research_questions: What share of checkout time goes to price queries at this store?

incremental.description: Stocker reports items whose search name or price is wrong.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the card terminal is already linked, so only price queries change, and stable prices keep queries few (s3 keeps 80) (1.7); high: item search answers most queries and the link removes card rekeying (8.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The stocker keeps the physical work: spotting damage, checking equipment, labelling and serving at the till. Paper logs, calculations and office re-keying drop out.
reach: Material movers' damage reports at the dock
skills_to_grow: Recording damage with clear reason codes and photos
Applying markdown rules and spotting when a rule is wrong
Reading the defect and damage view for their area
role.ambitious_version: A stocker who turns damage and near-expiry into vendor credit and timely markdowns the same day, and whose equipment reports drive planned maintenance.
